one_line: TrialBridge matches cancer patients to clinical trials through a WebMCP-enabled agent.
what_it_does: A patient-facing clinical-trial discovery workflow intended to reduce database searching and form burden.
leverage_rationale: Structured tools can ground trial search and matching in shared application state rather than fragile visual navigation; this is a substantial fit for a complex, high-stakes search workflow.
leverage_evidence: Pitch explicitly centers WebMCP-powered ChatGPT/Chrome agent matching patients to trials.
Frames show TrialBridge, registered webhooks, configuration screens, and safety/constraints UI.
execution_rationale: The packet shows a coherent branded product and multiple implementation/configuration surfaces, but no transcript or reliable end-to-end patient-to-trial result is demonstrated; dense frame evidence is hard to read.
execution_evidence: Devpost screenshot identifies TrialBridge and an embedded demo.
Frame sheets show a consistent dark product UI, webhook dashboard, code/editor work, and Safety & Constraints panel.
No video transcript and no clearly legible completed matching result.
impact_rationale: The intended audience—patients and care teams seeking scarce clinical-trial options—has a real, consequential access problem, and the proposed workflow directly addresses search friction and gatekeeping.
impact_evidence: About text describes geographic, knowledge, and usability barriers in clinical-trial access.
Pitch targets early therapy access for cancer patients.
creativity_rationale: Applying agent-native structured interaction to clinical-trial access is a meaningful and ambitious healthcare use case, though the core category is recognizable search/matching.
creativity_evidence: Combines patient trial matching with WebMCP agent interaction.
Packet visibly includes safety/constraints framing for the domain.
usability_note: The stated no-forms/no-endless-clicks goal is compelling, but the supplied visual evidence is too dense to assess the patient workflow clearly.
red_flags: Medical/high-stakes matching claims are not independently validated in the packet.
No end-to-end outcome or transcript is provided.
standouts: Strong real-world need.
Safety framing and structured-agent rationale are unusually relevant to the domain.
advance_reason: High-impact, strong WebMCP fit, and credible product intent merit advancement despite thin execution evidence.

one_line: Duel lets an external AI agent play four browser minigames through visible WebMCP calls.
what_it_does: A game arcade designed to make agent/page tool interaction observable, including a real-time Pong protocol demonstration.
leverage_rationale: The games enforce turn rules and shared live state through structured calls; the page-agent protocol is the central experience and is difficult to replicate comparably with generic visual driving.
leverage_evidence: Pitch states four minigames, every call visible live, and Pong over request/response.
About text describes enforced turns, shared board state, and page-registered tools.
Frames visibly show changing grid state, turn/status banners, and interactive game controls.
execution_rationale: The packet presents a coherent arcade with repeated interactive states and a clear visual progression, though completion/winner states are not visible and most text is low resolution.
execution_evidence: Frame sheets show consistent puzzle/game UI, changing board cells, status bars, and controls.
About describes Minesweeper, Connect 4, Pong, and Towers of Hanoi with concrete rules.
impact_rationale: The audience is educators, demonstrators, and curious users; it credibly makes an abstract protocol understandable, though direct practical impact is intentionally limited.
impact_evidence: About explicitly frames the goal as making WebMCP understandable in a room in under five minutes.
Visible game states make protocol behavior legible.
creativity_rationale: Using enforced games—including the ambitious claim of real-time Pong—to explain a page-as-tool protocol is a memorable and unusually effective interaction model.
creativity_evidence: Four-game arcade concept with an external agent opponent.
Real-time Pong over request/response is a surprising medium demonstration.
usability_note: Clear game framing and visible calls appear well suited to demonstration, though exact labels are not legible in the frame sheets.
red_flags: The packet lacks a transcript and a clearly visible final success state.
standouts: Protocol made concrete through rules and live game state.
Pong is an ambitious demonstration target.
advance_reason: Exceptional WebMCP-centered concept with strong visible execution and memorable creativity.

one_line: Agent Market lets buyer and seller agents negotiate a multidimensional deal before human confirmation.
what_it_does: A multi-vendor storefront where agents negotiate price, quantity, freebies, shipping, and coupons, while the user confirms the final order.
leverage_rationale: Negotiation requires shared structured state, repeated constrained turns, and precise mutation boundaries; WebMCP is central rather than a cosmetic action layer.
leverage_evidence: Pitch specifies buyer and store agents haggling over multiple deal dimensions through page tools.
About describes negotiation rounds, economic constraints, and a human Confirm dialog.
Frames show catalog UI and a consistent shopping product surface.
execution_rationale: The described architecture is unusually concrete, with one mutation path and explicit constraints; frames show a coherent catalog, though negotiation and confirmation are not directly visible in the contact sheets.
execution_evidence: About specifies Next.js/React, backend, OffersService.applyTurn, budget/floor constraints, and human confirmation.
Devpost screenshot visibly shows catalog, search/filtering, prices, discounts, and product cards.
impact_rationale: Shopping users have a clear desire to reduce tedious comparison and capture better multidimensional deals, while retaining final authority; the value is credible even for a niche marketplace.
impact_evidence: Pitch identifies price/quantity/add-on/shipping/coupon negotiation as the target burden.
Human confirmation addresses trust around purchase mutations.
creativity_rationale: Agent-to-agent haggling over a full deal, with a user-owned final confirmation, is a fresh and memorable interaction model beyond standard recommendation or checkout automation.
creativity_evidence: Buyer and store agents negotiate across several economic dimensions.
Human confirmation is built into the deal boundary.
usability_note: The catalog and explicit confirmation model suggest a clear user experience; the actual negotiation flow is not legible in the submitted sheets.
red_flags: The frame sheets mainly show catalog/registration states, not a completed negotiation transcript.
Claims of 95k+ real products are not independently evidenced.
standouts: Strong stateful WebMCP use case.
Thoughtful economic guardrails and human confirmation.
advance_reason: High leverage, strong concept originality, and credible implementation detail make this a top advancement candidate.

one_line: VirtuLab provides simulation workspaces where students and AI agents share experimental state.
what_it_does: An agent-native practical-learning platform with physics, chemistry, and other experiment workspaces.
leverage_rationale: Shared structured simulation state lets an agent reason over and manipulate experiments without guessing from pixels, materially changing tutoring and exploration.

execution_rationale: The packet shows a coherent onboarding-to-workspace flow and technical simulation/editor surfaces, but most frames repeat similar states and do not show a complete experiment outcome.

Devpost screenshot shows consistent VirtuLab branding and learning promise.

impact_evidence: About identifies the textbook-to-intuition gap and lack of daily practical lab access.

standouts: Strong shared-state education rationale.

one_line: ONCE coordinates one urgent story across four services while making disclosures and human approval visible.
what_it_does: A fictional essential-services planning demonstration that stages shelter, food, care, and mobility without sending actions before approval.
leverage_rationale: The value depends on shared structured state across multiple service tools, deterministic eligibility/conflict checks, field minimization, and explicit human authority; generic UI driving would be materially less reliable.
leverage_evidence: Pitch promises four coordinated services, visible disclosures, and final human action.
About describes deterministic eligibility checks, conflict avoidance, purpose-bound fields, blocked ID request, and one coordinated plan.
Frames show staged applications, validation, decision criteria, and conflict-free staging UI.
execution_rationale: The packet shows a coherent, polished staged-review workflow and multiple state/validation surfaces, but the demo link is dead and no transcript or live end-to-end execution is available.
execution_evidence: Devpost screenshot visibly shows service map, DATA OVERREACH BLOCKED, human gate, and metrics.
Frame sheets show Applications are staged, deterministic conflict-free staging, validation panels, and overwrite handling.

impact_evidence: About describes a concrete urgent family scenario and repeated storytelling problem.

creativity_rationale: The combination of one reusable life-event story, purpose-bound disclosure, cross-service conflict avoidance, and visible human authority is an original, ambitious service design.
creativity_evidence: Four-service coordination with blocked overreach and staged rather than executed actions.
Distinctive 'tell your story once' interaction model.
usability_note: The staged-review vocabulary and visible validation panels are coherent, but the dead demo link limits confidence in actual usability.
red_flags: Demo link is dead.
Services are fictional simulations and real-world effectiveness is not demonstrated.
standouts: Excellent consent/data-minimization framing.
High-stakes coordination is kept reversible and human-approved.

one_line: Trust Gateway inspects, minimizes, audits, and gates WebMCP tool calls between agents and sites.
what_it_does: A security and consent layer with tool metadata inspection, output-injection protection, parameter minimization, mutation approval, and visible auditing.
leverage_rationale: The product directly operates on the structured WebMCP surface and adds capabilities—inspection, provenance/risk checks, minimization, and per-call consent—that generic UI automation does not provide reliably.
leverage_evidence: About enumerates five controls applied to registered tools and outputs.
Frames visibly show Connected sites, Agent task, Trust/Tool log, warning states, monetary details, and approval controls.
Devpost preview shows inspected calls, quarantined output, and consent decisions.
execution_rationale: The dashboard, trust log, approval checkpoint, and expanded action details form a coherent security workflow with visible states; exact runtime behavior remains claimed rather than independently observed.
execution_evidence: Frame sheets show connected integrations, task launch, logged tool calls, risk/approval states, and approve/reject-style controls.
Devpost screenshot presents a consistent security dashboard and named controls.
impact_rationale: As agents gain ability to mutate website state, users and developers have a clear need for consent, least privilege, output-injection defense, and auditability.
impact_evidence: About identifies concrete risks: malicious tool metadata/output, excess personal data, and irreversible actions.
Visible dashboard centers human approval and transparent logging.
creativity_rationale: A dedicated trust/consent gateway for WebMCP is a timely and well-scoped infrastructure concept, pursued with multiple coordinated safeguards rather than a single approval dialog.
creativity_evidence: Five-control security model.
Per-call approval and quarantine/audit concepts are visibly integrated.
usability_note: The three-panel dashboard and visible trust log make oversight understandable; some labels and exact decisions are too small to verify.
red_flags: Displayed security metrics and blocked attacks may be simulated demo values.
No independent security testing is supplied.
standouts: Directly addresses the safety layer WebMCP needs.
Strong human-readable audit and consent model.
advance_reason: High leverage and impact with a coherent, visually evidenced security workflow.

leverage_rationale: The product directly expands WebMCP to legacy/authenticated sites while preserving the user’s browser session; this changes agent capability and reliability rather than merely automating an existing button.

execution_evidence: Frames visibly show AdapTab, Raising.fi example, structured amounts, browser visual-navigation contrast, and three trust boundaries.
Devpost screenshot clearly identifies the project and concept.

impact_rationale: Agents currently cannot use most legacy/authenticated sites reliably; a reusable adapter layer could unlock broad practical utility while reducing visual navigation cost and credential export.
impact_evidence: About targets legacy/authenticated platforms and missing WebMCP coverage.

standouts: Potentially foundational WebMCP adoption layer.
